subject.title: Plugin installs crash Express 4.x routes: core npm-shrinkwrap pins path-to-regexp@8.x but no central override covers plugins

question: Should managed npm plugin roots inherit OpenClaw workspace overrides like path-to-regexp, or should OpenClaw scope/exempt those overrides so plugin-owned dependency graphs can resolve their own router stack?
rationale: The source-level bug is clear, but the fix changes a dependency ownership and supply-chain boundary for all npm-installed plugins, and the obvious blanket downgrade conflicts with OpenClaw's own Express 5 stack.

options.title: Scope managed-root overrides
options.body: Keep security-critical host override support, but add a maintainer-approved exception or scoped policy so Express 4 plugin trees can resolve path-to-regexp 0.1.x while core keeps 8.x.

options.title: Validator-only guidance
options.body: Detect Express 4 plus a conflicting path-to-regexp resolution during install/update and fail with a clear override or upgrade message, accepting that plugin authors still own the package fix.

options.title: Plugin-owned only
options.body: Keep current override propagation and document that affected plugin packages must ship their own overrides or migrate to Express 5, leaving this class outside core repair.

recommendation.title: Scope managed-root overrides
recommendation.body: Keep security-critical host override support, but add a maintainer-approved exception or scoped policy so Express 4 plugin trees can resolve path-to-regexp 0.1.x while core keeps 8.x.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the strongest current-history connection to managed npm install and override propagation.
